SOLAR THERMAL ENERGY

Sunlight, directed
towards industrial heat.

Solar thermal systems collect solar energy as heat for suitable industrial processes. Integration starts with the heat demand.

Discuss your application↗

Solar Thermal Energy

Understanding before selection.

01

Heat from sunlight

Solar thermal collectors absorb solar radiation and transfer energy to a working fluid. Unlike photovoltaic systems, their principal output is thermal energy rather than electricity.

02

Match collection to demand

Collector choice depends on the required temperature, local solar resource, operating schedule and site constraints. Concentrating and non-concentrating systems address different conditions.

03

Transfer heat where it is useful

Piping, heat exchangers and controls connect collection to the process. The integration point should match the required supply temperature and return conditions.

04

Consider thermal storage

Storage can shift some collected heat to another time. Its useful capacity and losses must be assessed against the daily load profile; storage does not eliminate every supply mismatch.

05

Plan industrial integration

Potential uses include water preheating, washing and drying where temperatures and operating schedules are suitable. Existing heat recovery opportunities should be considered alongside solar integration.

06

Evaluate the opportunity

Technical feasibility and environmental benefit depend on the full system, including backup heat, auxiliary energy, maintenance and operating conditions. Discuss the application before assuming a performance or savings figure.

A MATERIAL JOURNEY

From radiation to process.

  5. 05
